steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
Place 1 crust in the bottom of a 9-inch pie pan.
Combine sugar, flour, and cinnamon in a bowl. Mix lightly through strawberries.
Pour filling into the pastry-lined pan and dot with butter pieces.
Cover with top crust and cut slits in the top to vent. Seal and flute the edges.
Bake in the preheated oven until the crust is slightly browned, 35 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-Fashioned Strawberry Pie
raw_recipe.description: A wonderful old-fashioned strawberry pie recipe made with fresh strawberries piled into a prepared crust and baked for an easy summer dessert.

review.reviewBody:
There are so many reviews on this pie, and unfortunately there ae a few that are not praises. This pie, as with anything that a good cook knows, must have a little personal tweek if you are that kind of a cook, but I have been not only professionally trained, but I am a very good cook and I will tell you this basic recipe is unbelievably good and shockingly easy and above all it will bring you praise. I followed the recipe--I was busy and lazy, but it still brought me rave reviews. Sweetness is personal.....think about your berries and taste them, then decide. Think about other pies you have made and what thickener do you like the best. If it is tapioca, use it in the proportions you are used too, if it is flour use the flour, but if you want to make sure a pie is thick then add a tad more. If you make the pie and you had problems then you must realize it may not be the recipes fault, but your own for now thinking things out.

This pie is excellent as it stands....the taste is sweet, it is not too thick of a mixture around the berries when finished and couple those things with a very good crust and people will shout praise. Try the milk on the crust route sprinkled with sugar and it will put the Sunday clothes on the pie.....thicken with tapioca if you want a clearer thicker, more stable pie.......and if you want that great taste and sight is secondary to taste then you are find to head on and serve your family the pie as it is written.

This pie turned out beautiful! I used frozen strawberries instead of fresh and also added 3 tablespoons of cornstarch to thicken the recipe. I cut the sugar down to 3/4 cup as some recommended; i'd actually prefer it a bit sweeter cuz my berries turned out to be tart. For sweet, fresh berries, 3/4 cup of sugar is probably fine, tho. I brushed the top crust with half&half and sprinkled it with sugar so it turned a shiny golden brown. This is a very good pie... i would make it again! :D

I've never baked a strawberry pie, but had 4 quarts of strawberries given to me. I read all of the reviews and took some advice. I halved my strawberries and used maybe 6 cups measured after halved. I used 3/4 cup of white sugar and 1/4 cup of brown sugar. I added 3 TBSP cornstarch. I had a prepackaged crust on hand from Trader Joe's that I rolled out. It is an adequate pie crust but not very big. I did take the advice to bake at 425 for 25 minutes and then switched to 350 degrees. I swear it took at least 1 solid hour AFTER i turned it down to 350! But I cooled the pie outside at night for an hour and then switched it to the fridge for 1 1/2 hours. I couldn't believe my eyes when it came out in a solid piece and did not run! My husband raved about it being one of the best fruit pies he'd ever had. It was just the right amount of sugar, too. I think next time, since after 25 minutes at 425 the crust was barely beginning to color, I'd wait for more color before turning the oven temp down. I was wondering if it was too dry. Either too much corn starch or too long in the oven. But either way, I was very pleased with the results! Will keep it and make it again! And use more strawberries next time! I used the amount to be level with my pie pan. It sunk down a little as it cooled. Next time I will heap them up in the center.

I loved this recipe. I did a couple of things different though. I cubed up 8 oz of cream cheese (let get to room temperature first) with the strawberries and sugar in a pot and heat until all was mixed well and the berries released the juice, then added the cinnamon, then added a 2 TBSP of cornstarch for thickening (I like a thicker pie filling, I mixed it with maybe 1/3 cup cold water before adding). I then poured the mixture into my crust, added my top crust, brushed with milk and sprinkled with sugar, then baked for 45 minutes at 350. Turned out beautifully. I do realize my lattice crust isn't perfect lol

This will be my go to recipe for two crust strawberry pie. I read a few reviews before starting. I made a couple of tweaks. I added one tablespoon of cornstarch to the flour. I used one cup of sugar because my berries were sweet. I let the strawberry mixture sit while I rolled the pastry and put it in the pie plate. Quite a bit of juice came out so I drained some leaving the mixture juicy but not swimming in it. The pie was delicious!

This is an awesome pie. I did make a few changes. Reading most of the reviews I was concerned I would end up with strawberry soup pie so in addition to the 1/4 cup flour I also added 1/3 cup corn starch. When I added the flour, corn starch and sugar I mixed them by hand using some kitchen latex gloves so as not to end up smashing the berries with a spoon. I cut the larger berries into 1/2 the size. I also left out the butter and cinnamon because I did not want to take away the taste of the fruit. The pie came out absolutely perfect as far as consistency goes. Not soupy at all yet not gelled either. Great recipe just make sure you use more thickening agent than the original recipe called for. Will definitely make it again.

I read other reviews before beginning because the recipe seemed too simple for someone like me who usually needs a hand hold. The key to having a thick pie that doesn't run is cooking the filling in a pan first, on medium low to low heat! My strawberries were a bit on the tart side, so I stuck with the cup of sugar. I decided against the cinnamon all together, and instead went with a tiny splash of vanilla and juice from half a small lemon. I also bumped up the flower to a 1/2 cup, but when you cook it all together on low heat, you may not need that much. Recipe definitely calls for whipped cream on top! will definitely keep baking and experimenting, but i think cooking is the key

Thank you for sharing this recipe, it is the best strawberry pie I've ever made. I did reduce the sugar down to 1c, pre reviews and baked 425 for 25 min and 350 for the last 15, it came out perfect. This will be the one I made from now on.

Delicious! Included picture of day 2 of the pie and it’s still beautiful - used fresh strawberries 3/4 cup sugar, 1 tbsp corn starch and 3/4 cup flour. Made a crumble top instead of the top crust, baked as instructed.

I loved this pie! I used fresh, sweet strawberries, so I took the sugar down to 3/4 cup. I adjusted a few others things too- 5 tbsp of cornstarch instead of 1/3 cup flour, reduced cinnamon to 1/4 tsp, and added 1 tbsp lemon juice. I also did a lattice top rather than a full crust. I baked it for 80 minutes at 375F. The pie was delicious and not runny at all!
It was runny, and the crust browned too fast. I would add more flour and cook at a lower temperature.
followed recipe except flower I added 2 tablespoons of flour. DELISH.

I made the pie per recipe, except I cut the sugar back to 3/4 of a cup and did not use any cinnamon. The pie went together well. I even did not mix the strawberries and the dry ingredients together until I have the bottom crust in place. I was hoping not to have a runny pie. Oh I did add 2 tablespoons of cornstarch. I baked it for 35 minutes but halfway through, I realized the flutes were browning too quickly. I covered them with aluminum foil and bake the pie the rest of the time. The outside of the pie looks very good. I allowed it to cool about an hour on the counter and then put it in the refrigerator for eight hours. The pie was then served and I was disappointed that it was somewhat runny. The taste, however, with some whipped cream, was delicious. The bottom crust I found to be a little doughy, though, which didn’t surprise me with as runny as the pie was. I doubt I make this pie again.
Way too much liquid. As others have said it needs cornstarch to thicken. Also the sugar needs to be reduced.
It was easy to make, and when it was cool we served it with a scoop of vanilla ice-cream, it was so delicious.
Very tasty. However very runny. Needs a thickener or so a cornstarch slurry with the ingredients so it's thicker

Reiterating tweaks mentioned: cornstarch, more strawberries (at least two cups), half sugar, no quartering the berries (halve them, only if approaching golf ball size). Agree with altering heat for browning.. ie half hour overall, 425 for initial 10. (Alternative *might* be to finish off with a 2 minute broil.. I intend to try it next time.) Pre-baking bottom crust recommended. Just my impression-- strawberry seems like a fruit pie to NOT bake until juice shows through the crust. Too easy to overcook. Less is more.
So good

I love baking, but this is the first pie I've made. The only problem I ran into was that the pie bubbled over some, but I might have made a mistake on the strawberry measurement. I have done that before. My grandmother always says to follow the recipe the first time you bake something and make it your own the second time. So I might make some changes the next time, but it is delicious as is.

Absolutely delicious! I've been making strawberry pies for most of my long life and this VERY simple to make pie is, without doubt, the best. I did not have to alter anything in the recipe but a few things could be clearer. First, the four cups of strawberries present as a very flat to underfilled pie. I added a large number of whole berries to the top to give it that fuller appearance. Second, the ingredients you toss the berries in should all be added to the pie, not discarded. If you do so, your pie will be runny. Simply put the berries in first and then continue to shake the powder over the berries in the pie shell until it uses all of the remaining materials. The pie itself is sweet, deliciously so, and I had only average berries, so don't add sugar past the amount in the recipe unless you are positive the berries are tart. A tip that is tried and true? Before you place the bottom crust, rub flour heavily onto both sides of it. The flour prevents any fruit from saturating the bottom crust and helps thicken the filling a little more. I'm always shocked at the difference this makes, so if you are tired of doughy bottom crusts try this. Enjoy! It is an excellent and simple way to make a pie they will remember.
